issues.issue: This recital states the Depositor "is the owner of the Trust Fund that is hereby conveyed to the Trustee," which cannot be squared with Section 2.01 and Section 2.06, under which the conveyance is made by separate operative granting clauses and the Special Deposit is transferred by EMC rather than the Depositor. A party could argue the recital controls the scope of what passed to the Trustee.

The REMIC I pool is described as the Mortgage Loans "and certain other related assets subject to this Agreement," a phrase with no ascertainable boundary, followed by a closed list of exclusions. Which trust assets fall inside REMIC I is left to construction.

The provision invokes Treasury Regulation Section 1.860G-1(a)(4)(ii) while the accompanying maturity-date designation and every parallel REMIC paragraph invoke Section 1.860G-1(a)(4)(iii). The mismatched citation changes which regulatory safe harbor is being satisfied.

The paragraph makes the REMIC III election but designates the segregated pool of REMIC II Regular Interests as "REMIC II" rather than REMIC III. As written, two different asset pools bear the same designation.

The Class R-3 Certificates are said to be the sole class of Residual Interests in "REMIC II," although the definition of Class R-3 Certificate makes them the residual interest in REMIC III and the Class R-2 Certificates already hold REMIC II's residual. The designation contradicts itself.

Every defined term is made defeasible by the phrase "unless the context otherwise requires," with no guide to when context displaces a definition. That qualifier is itself the ground on which a party can argue a defined term does not mean what Article I says.

"Accepted Master Servicing Practices" is measured by the "customary mortgage servicing practices of prudent mortgage servicing institutions" in the relevant jurisdiction, a standard the Agreement never fixes or benchmarks. The parenthetical carve-out "(except in its capacity as successor to a Servicer)" further leaves unclear which standard governs when the Master Servicer succeeds a Servicer.

"Adjustment Date" is fixed as the first day of the month in which the Mortgage Rate changes, which may not be the adjustment date actually stated in the related Mortgage Note. Which date governs rate resets is therefore open to argument.

"Appraised Value" uses the refinancing appraisal alone for refinance loans but the lesser of appraisal and sales price for other loans, whereas the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement defines "Value" as always the lesser of appraisal and sales price. The two measures drive different loan-to-value figures for the same loans.

The definition identifies the underlying Accredited and WMC purchase and warranties agreements as "each between the Sponsor and Accredited" and "each between the Sponsor and WMC," while the bring-down letters it lists in the same clauses are with EMC. Which entity made the incorporated originator representations is left contradictory.

Certificate Principal Balance is increased by Subsequent Recoveries "pursuant to Section 5.04(b)," but Section 5.04 is the Yield Maintenance Credit Support Annex and loss/recovery allocation is dealt with in Article VI. The cross-reference does not lead to any recovery mechanic.

The Class A-3 Certificate is defined as representing the right to the Percentage Interest of "distributions provided for the Class A-2 Certificates," not the Class A-3 Certificates. On its face the definition gives Class A-3 holders another class's distribution entitlement.

This definition reduces the Stated Principal Balance for "Realized Losses incurred during the prior calendar month," whereas the parallel Class M-1, M-2, M-3 and M-5 definitions use Realized Losses incurred "during the related Prepayment Period." The two measurement periods produce different principal distribution amounts.

Clause (x) lists the Class A, M-1, M-2, M-4 and M-5 Principal Distribution Amounts but omits the Class M-3 Principal Distribution Amount, although clause (y)(4) still accounts for the Class M-3 balance after its distribution. The omission changes the remaining Principal Distribution Amount available to Class M-6.

The Class P Certificate Account is said to be established "pursuant to Section 6.09 hereof," but the Agreement's Article VI ends at Section 6.08, which is itself captioned "Class P Certificate Account." The account's governing section is left uncertain.
